subject.title: Bug:  ignores  config and returns success on media failure

question: Should Feishu outbound media use a Feishu-specific local-root config now, or wait for the shared filesystem/media-root policy before changing allowed host-file reads and upload-failure semantics?
rationale: The source-level problem is real, but the fix changes both host-file read permissions and user-visible fallback behavior, so code alone cannot safely choose the permanent security and product contract.

options.title: Use shared root contract first
options.body: Route Feishu through the canonical shared media/filesystem root policy, then make allowlist failures visibly fail or visibly report partial success with regression tests.

options.title: Add Feishu-specific roots
options.body: Accept a narrow Feishu-owned `mediaLocalRoots` config surface now, with explicit security docs, tests for allowed and denied paths, and no `any` bypass outside the safe reader contract.

options.title: Preserve fallback only
options.body: Keep current root behavior and fallback text delivery, but document the staging directories and ensure the CLI says the media upload degraded rather than reporting a normal attachment send.

recommendation.title: Use shared root contract first
recommendation.body: Route Feishu through the canonical shared media/filesystem root policy, then make allowlist failures visibly fail or visibly report partial success with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses shared outbound media access and Feishu plugin behavior, and this owner has recent history on the shared access plumbing.
